scenarios.name: hits-throughput
scenarios.purpose: 100,000 keys that fit in the cache, zero-cost solver, TTL 60 s, 4 s warm-up so the whole trace is seen before measuring: the steady-state hit path and lock contention from 1 to 16 workers.

scenarios.name: eviction-churn
scenarios.purpose: 1,000,000 keys, Zipf 0.8, capacity 10,000, 1 ms solver, 16 workers: miss-heavy traffic with constant LRU eviction; solver calls versus misses show how many concurrent misses on the same key were coalesced. The solver sleeps 1 ms rather than less because Go's time.Sleep rounds sub-millisecond sleeps up to about 1 ms on Linux; the measured mean solver time is reported for both implementations.

scenarios.name: cold-herd
scenarios.purpose: 100 keys, uniform, 64 workers, 50 ms solver, no warm-up: a cold start where every worker asks for keys nobody has computed yet. With single-flight the solver runs exactly 100 times; without it, up to 64 times per key.

scenarios.name: hot-cold-ttl
scenarios.purpose: 200,000 keys, Zipf 1.0, 2 ms solver, TTL 1 s, 16 workers: both libraries renew the TTL on every hit (sliding expiration), so popular keys stay cached while keys requested less than once per second expire and are recomputed; measures a self-balancing mix of sub-microsecond hits and 2 ms recomputations.
